# utils/ledgers/quarantine.txt — the findings of the quarantine plugin and the opt-out regions in each file, kind and
# entity.
#
# The rule quarantine reads this ledger (`python3 utils/bin/guard explain quarantine`).  Its module
# utils/assay/guard/engines/plugin/quarantine.py writes each row through utils/assay/core/ledger.py.  Do not edit a
# count row by hand.  The rule reads the section .crucible.quarantine of each object of the target all, and it counts each
# finding line one time.  A count above its row fails the rule, because a change can only lower a count (rule R11 of
# misc/01_10_2026_quarantine.md).  So a change that removes std::vector from a file and adds std::map to it fails.  A
# file that the ledger does not hold and that has a finding fails too: a new file has no finding.  A count below its
# row also fails, until the same commit writes the rows again:
#     python3 utils/bin/guard write --rule quarantine --build-dir build
# On a merge conflict in this file, take the version of main, build, and write the rows again.
#
# THE ROWS (the rows grammar of utils/assay/core/rows.py)
#   configuration NAME KEY VALUE   A build that counts: the build kind and the target tier of
#                                  utils/assay/core/target.py, and each cache variable that changes
#                                  the objects of all or their preprocessor arms.  NAME is the build
#                                  kind, with -bench and -fuzz for those options.  The first
#                                  configuration is the base.
#   reason PREFIX | REASON         The reason of each count row of a file under PREFIX: the step of
#                                  the plan that removes its findings.  A person writes these rows,
#                                  and a write removes a row that holds no count row (THE REASON OF
#                                  A PREFIX of utils/assay/core/ledger.py).
#   FILE | KIND | COUNT | ENTITY | -
#                                  The number of findings of the kind KIND and the entity ENTITY in
#                                  the file, in the base configuration.  A file of the build
#                                  directory has the prefix @build/.  The head comment of
#                                  utils/tools/quarantine/plugin.h gives the kinds, and THE ENTITY
#                                  of utils/assay/guard/engines/plugin/quarantine.py gives the
#                                  entity of each kind.  The entity holds no line, so a move of
#                                  code keeps each row.  A kind with no entity has the cell "-".
#   @NAME | FILE | KIND | DELTA | ENTITY | -
#                                  The count of the configuration NAME, as a difference from the
#                                  base count (+N or -N).
#
# THE OPT-OUT REGIONS
#   A finding in an opt-out region has the kind opted-out, and its entity is "REASON | KIND
#   ENTITY": the reason of the region, and the kind and the entity of the finding.  A cell writes
#   the bar of that entity as \|.  So these rows hold what each region covers.  A row of the kind
#   region counts the regions of the file with the reason of its entity.  A region that covers
#   more, and a new region, fail the rule until
#       python3 utils/bin/guard write --rule quarantine --build-dir build --admit
#   writes the new count.  Use --admit only for a region of a reason class of CLAUDE.md section
#   XXII, and give the reason in the commit.  The rule history gives a warning for each such
#   count on each run.  Only a region that a build compiles has a row.
#
# THE TIER
#   The tier names the target of the build flags.  When a compile of the objects of all has its own
#   -march=native or -mcpu=native, the tier adds "+" and the native tier of the host.  The units of
#   test/layer/admitted_flag_matrix compile with the release flags, and each bench target adds
#   -march=native, so each x86_64 configuration here has the native tier of the build host.  A
#   build on a different processor can compile other preprocessor arms, for example the AVX-512 arm
#   of include/crucible/SwissTable.h.  The rows of its name judge it, and a line names its tier, so
#   a finding of such an arm fails it.
#
# THE CONFIGURATIONS
#   x86_64-debug-asan              The default preset, in the build directory build.  The base.
#   x86_64-release                 The release preset (build-release).
#   x86_64-debug-asan-bench-fuzz   The default preset with CRUCIBLE_BENCH=ON and CRUCIBLE_FUZZ=ON:
#                                      cmake --preset default -B build-extended -DCRUCIBLE_BENCH=ON
#                                      -DCRUCIBLE_FUZZ=ON
#                                  The CI job fuzz builds it.
#   x86_64-debug-tsan              The tsan preset (build-tsan).  Its preprocessor arms of
#                                  __SANITIZE_THREAD__, such as the routes of
#                                  src/foundation/os/Intercepted.cpp, count here.
#   aarch64-...                    The default and the release preset on aarch64.  Only CI builds
#                                  them.  The leg writes the rows of its configuration after a
#                                  failure of the rule and when the ledger does not hold it, each
#                                  after the mark "ledger-row: ", and
#                                      python3 utils/bin/guard write --rule quarantine --import LOG
#                                  puts them here.
#   The rows of the configuration with the name of a build judge it, and a line names each fact
#   of the configuration that the build does not share.  The largest count of each key over the
#   configurations judges a build of a name that the ledger does not hold, and no build skips the
#   rule (THE POLICY of utils/assay/core/configuration.py).  An arm that a configuration here
#   counts then passes, and a new finding fails.
#   A change that lowers a count in each configuration writes only the base rows.  A change of a
#   file or an arm that only a later configuration compiles writes that configuration too, with
#   `guard write` in its build directory.  A change of the keys of the base makes this file again:
#   keep this head, remove the rows, and write each configuration with --add-configuration in its
#   build directory, the base first.
#   The vessel units that need PyTorch compile only when TORCH_DIR is set.  No configuration sets
#   TORCH_DIR, so the ledger does not count those units.  The rows of its name judge a build with
#   TORCH_DIR, so the findings of those units fail it.
#   No configuration turns on CRUCIBLE_SENSE_HUB_V2.  Each build compiles the SenseHub v2 sources
#   in two object libraries that no target links, with and without CRUCIBLE_SENSE_HUB_EXTENDED
#   (CMakeLists.txt), so these rows count each arm of those sources.  The UBSan-strict, verify,
#   bench and PGO presets are no configuration.  The largest counts judge their builds, so a
#   finding of an arm that only they compile fails them.
format 1
rule quarantine
